newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Nepal set to sign energy transfer pact.
newsitem.headline: India, Nepal set to sign energy transfer pact.

text.p: India and Nepal expect to sign a pathbreaking agreement on energy trade and power-sharing within three weeks, a senior Indian diplomat said on Friday.

"The power trade agreement permitting private developers to generate power in Nepal and export it to anyone in India will be signed fairly soon," India's Ambassador to Nepal K.V. Rajan told a meeting of businessmen.

Rajan, who was accompanying Nepali Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand on a one-day visit to India's commercial capital, told Reuters later that the agreement would be signed within three weeks' time.
Chand appealed to Indian business to invest in the Himalayan country, which offers opportunities for ventures in power and tourism.

"We have invited Indian investments in joint ventures in industrial fields in Nepal so as to develop and diversify our exportable products in Nepal for our mutual benefit," Chand told the Confederation of Indian Industry, a club of businessmen.
"It is high time that two friendly countries, India and Nepal should make efforts to increase our bilateral and regional trade for the benefit of our two countries and our region."
India and Nepal have taken numerous initiatives to boost bilateral trade during the last few years, businessmen travelling with Chand said.

"A recent treaty between the two countries means that goods manufactured in Nepal can get differential access to the Indian market without duty payment," said C.L. Agarwal, of the Federation of Nepali Chambers of Commerce and Industry.

"This is an encouragement to Indian firms to set up manufacturing bases in Nepal which will give them access not just to the Nepali market of 20 million but also to others across the region," he added.
Rajan said Nepal had identified 100 sites suitable for power plants and these would be offered for development after feasibility studies had been completed.
Liberal new rules would prompt Indian businessmen to invest in Nepal, he said.
"The liberalisation of investment regulations permits Indian businessmen to invest up to 250 million rupees ($6.97 million) into Nepal on a more-or-less automatic basis," Rajan said.
"Larger sums can also be approved on a fast track basis."
India plans to open new air routes to Nepal, Rajan added.
"Air-India will start flights between Bombay and Kathmandu soon," he said. "Indian Airlines is also scheduled to start a flight."
